description: Guide the student to collect realtime market updates from a streaming endpoint (or polling fallback), store timestamped updates as a CSV file, and teach quant microstructure/data-quality concepts (trade vs quote, bid-ask spread, latency/out-of-order ticks, and market-hours timezone handling). Evaluation in this Track A task is hybrid: tutor output quality plus runnable-code evidence from tool logs.

student_openings.beginner_no_finance: Can you help me write code to capture live market updates and save them to CSV? I also want to understand why realtime data can be noisy or misleading.
student_openings.intermediate_developer: I need a practical realtime ingestion example (streaming endpoint or polling fallback) plus quant checks for out-of-order ticks, timezone normalization, and market-hours filtering.
student_openings.advanced_quant: I want an execution-ready realtime capture script (quote/trade stream to CSV) and a teaching walkthrough on microstructure caveats: bid-ask spread, latency, stale ticks, and session boundaries.

ground_truth.expected_outcome: Tutor provides persona-adapted instruction quality for realtime ingestion, demonstrates runnable code execution, and clearly explains quant microstructure caveats: trade-vs-quote semantics, bid-ask spread context, latency/out-of-order risks, and timezone/session handling.

required_capabilities.description: Adapts explanation depth to learner level
required_capabilities.evidence: beginner receives plain-language scaffolding, intermediate receives implementation-oriented guidance, advanced receives microstructure-level caveats

required_capabilities.description: Explains quote vs trade semantics and spread context
required_capabilities.evidence: distinguishes quote/trade meaning and mentions bid/ask or spread
mentions stale/out-of-order ticks plus timezone/session boundaries (UTC or exchange hours)
gives concrete checks or checklist to verify realtime stream quality
